grammar.name: Passato prossimo with avere
grammar.scope: formation with avere + regular past participles (-ato, -uto, -ito); ieri, la settimana scorsa

chapters.theme: Buying and renovating a house; the builders
chapters.a_plot: The Carters have bought Via dei Tigli 14. Chiara has designed a new kitchen; Ben has hired the builders. Everyone recounts to Franco what they did, and Franco asks why nobody asked him.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo tells Nadia what he did with the bar's money this month. Nadia checks the numbers.
chapters.arc: Season premiere: the renovation arc begins.

grammar.name: Irregular past participles
grammar.scope: fatto, detto, preso, messo, visto, scritto, letto, aperto, chiuso, rotto, chiesto, risposto, perso, bevuto

chapters.a_plot: Day one of the works: the builders open the wrong wall, the water is off, and nobody admits to anything. Ben investigates.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto has 'seen everything' and has written it all down in a notebook.
chapters.runner: The builders' foreman, Sergio, says 'Nessun problema' before every problem.

grammar.name: Passato prossimo with essere
grammar.scope: verbs of motion and change (andare, venire, arrivare, partire, uscire, entrare, tornare, restare, nascere, morire, diventare); participle agreement

chapters.theme: Trips, arriving and leaving, a day out
chapters.a_plot: The Carters escape the dust of the renovation with a day in Monza: the Villa Reale park, bikes, and nobody arriving where they planned to.
chapters.b_plot: Emma didn't go: she 'stayed home to study'. She actually went skateboarding with Tommaso. Ornella saw her leave.

grammar.name: Passato prossimo of reflexive verbs
grammar.scope: reflexives always take essere; agreement (mi sono alzata); common reflexives in the past

chapters.a_plot: Ben oversleeps and misses the builders, Leo's school trip and a meeting with Roberto's committee. He has to explain himself to everyone.
chapters.b_plot: Franco and Lucia tell Leo the story of how they met at the dance class ('Ci siamo conosciuti per caso...').
chapters.runner: Excuses at school: Leo's 'my cat ate my homework' doesn't work (he doesn't have a cat).

grammar.name: Past time expressions
grammar.scope: fa, già, ancora (non), appena, sempre, mai with passato prossimo; scorso; position of adverbs with compound tenses

chapters.a_plot: The whole ensemble's Easter Monday picnic by the lake. Who has already brought the food, who hasn't yet, who has just forgotten the blanket.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia has been strange all day: she hasn't eaten Samira's food, which she never refuses. Samira notices.
chapters.arc: Tentpole: the whole cast in one place. The pregnancy is planted.

grammar.name: Direct object pronouns
grammar.scope: mi, ti, lo, la, ci, vi, li, le; position before conjugated verbs and attached to infinitives; lo so / non lo so

chapters.a_plot: Nadia is pregnant. She tells Matteo at the worst possible moment: during the Milan–Inter derby at the bar.
chapters.b_plot: The news travels down Via dei Tigli in one afternoon. Everybody knows it, and nobody says they know it.

grammar.name: Object pronouns with passato prossimo
grammar.scope: l'ho visto/vista, li ho presi, le ho perse; agreement of the participle with lo/la/li/le

chapters.theme: Lost and found; looking for things
chapters.a_plot: Franco has lost Anna's ring. The whole family searches the house and the orto, and nobody has seen it.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo panics about being a father and looks for 'the manual'. Nadia hides the books he bought.
chapters.runner: Pavarotti the cat is found in the builders' cement bag.
chapters.arc: Planted: Franco wants the ring for Lucia (it pays off with the S3 proposal).

grammar.name: Indirect object pronouns
grammar.scope: mi, ti, gli, le, Le, ci, vi, gli; verbs with indirect objects (dire, dare, scrivere, telefonare, regalare, chiedere, rispondere)

chapters.theme: Communication: phones, messages, the family WhatsApp group
chapters.a_plot: Chiara creates a family WhatsApp group. Franco sends 40 voice messages a day; Ben replies with the wrong emoji.
chapters.b_plot: Tommaso writes Emma a message and doesn't send it for three days. Bianca sends it for him.
chapters.runner: Leo sends a voice message to the whole class parents' group by mistake.

grammar.name: Piacere in the past; verbs like piacere
grammar.scope: mi è piaciuto/a/i/e; mancare, servire, sembrare, interessare, bastare, restare

chapters.a_plot: Ben has a bad week: he misses Chicago, his friends, his job and feeling competent. It's Ornella, of all people, who notices.
chapters.b_plot: Emma, who spent all of Season 1 wanting to go back, realises she doesn't miss Chicago as much as she thought.

grammar.name: Ci (there); ci vuole / ci vogliono
grammar.scope: ci as 'there' (ci vado, ci sono stato); ci vuole / ci vogliono for time and things needed; ci metto

chapters.a_plot: The works stop: the committee (Roberto) says the new window needs a permit. Ben goes to the town hall's technical office, then again, then again.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara discovers the permit problem in the family chat and sends Ben 14 messages from Milan.
chapters.runner: Sergio the foreman: 'Nessun problema. Ci vogliono due settimane.' (It takes two months.)

grammar.name: Ne (partitive)
grammar.scope: ne for quantities (ne voglio due, non ne ho); ne with passato prossimo (ne ho comprati tre)

chapters.theme: Recipes, quantities, the bar's orders and supplies
chapters.a_plot: Matteo orders supplies for the bar wrong: 300 croissants and no coffee. Ben helps him count, measure and fix it.
chapters.b_plot: Samira teaches Nadia to make msemen for 'the baby's grandmother's recipe collection'. Lucia wants to teach her tiramisù on the same day.
chapters.runner: Leo counts everything: 'Quante uova ci sono?' 'Ce ne sono dodici.'

grammar.name: Stressed (tonic) pronouns
grammar.scope: me, te, lui, lei, Lei, noi, voi, loro after prepositions and for emphasis (per me, con te, anche lui, tocca a te)

chapters.theme: Work and jobs; behind the bar counter
chapters.a_plot: Matteo offers Ben a morning job at Bar Tigli. Ben behind the counter: the regulars test him, Ornella watches him, Franco refuses to be served by him.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara is proud of Ben and worried about what her colleagues will think ('Mio marito fa il barista?'). She hates herself for thinking it.
chapters.arc: Tentpole: Ben gets a job. He becomes the street's confidant.

grammar.name: Reciprocal verbs
grammar.scope: ci/vi/si + verb for 'each other' (ci vediamo, si conoscono, si sono sposati, ci scriviamo)

chapters.a_plot: Emma and Tommaso start 'seeing each other' but keep it secret: they meet at the station, write to each other at night and say hello coldly on the street.
chapters.b_plot: Lucia and Franco want to go public on Via dei Tigli. They walk arm in arm to the bar, where everyone is waiting.
chapters.runner: Ben and Roberto greet each other with maximum politeness and minimum warmth.

grammar.name: Double negatives
grammar.scope: non... mai, più, niente/nulla, nessuno, ancora, neanche; nessun/nessuna + noun; negatives at the start of a sentence

chapters.a_plot: The renovation crisis: nothing works, nobody answers, the new oven has never worked. Ben calls customer service, in Italian, on hold for an hour.
chapters.b_plot: Chiara, stressed by the works and by Milan, snaps at everyone. Franco tells her she's just like her mother. It's meant as a compliment.
chapters.runner: Sergio doesn't come to work any more; nobody knows where he is.

grammar.name: Formal and informal address
grammar.scope: Lei with verbs, pronouns and possessives (Suo, La, Le); tu vs Lei choices; formal greetings; 'darsi del tu' as a social event

chapters.theme: Politeness, formal and informal situations, etiquette
chapters.a_plot: Ornella's birthday. Ben brings her a cake he made himself, and after eight months of 'Signora Galli', she says: 'Diamoci del tu, Ben.'
chapters.b_plot: Leo uses 'tu' with Maestra Paola's headmaster and 'Lei' with his friend Pietro. A lesson in registers.
chapters.arc: Tentpole: the Lei → tu moment with Ornella.

title.en: Italy or America: Which Is Better?

grammar.name: Comparatives
grammar.scope: più/meno ... di / che; (così) ... come, (tanto) ... quanto; più di/che rules with nouns, adjectives, verbs

chapters.a_plot: Leo's school presentation: 'L'Italia e l'America'. He interviews the family and every answer turns into an argument between Franco and Ben about which is better.
chapters.b_plot: Matteo compares himself to every father he knows, and always comes out worse.
chapters.runner: Is American coffee coffee? The debate at the bar lasts all episode.

title.it: Il tiramisù più buono del mondo
title.en: The Best Tiramisù in the World

grammar.name: Superlatives
grammar.scope: relative superlative (il più ... di); absolute -issimo; irregular forms migliore, peggiore, ottimo, pessimo, maggiore, minore

chapters.a_plot: Matteo organises a tiramisù contest at the bar. Lucia enters with Anna's recipe, Samira with her own version, and Ben with a 'reinvented' one.
chapters.b_plot: Franco is the judge, and must choose between his late wife's recipe made by his girlfriend and everyone else.
chapters.runner: Ornella rates everything 'discreto', the highest compliment she gives.

grammar.name: Adverbs: -mente; molto, tanto, troppo, poco
grammar.scope: forming adverbs in -mente; bene/male; molto/tanto/troppo/poco as adjectives (agreeing) vs adverbs (invariable)

chapters.a_plot: Franco's bocce team needs a fourth player for the spring tournament. The only one available is Ben.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia's doctor tells her to slow down; she doesn't know how. Matteo tries to do everything for her, too fast and too much.

grammar.name: Duration: da, per, fa
grammar.scope: present + da for ongoing actions (abito qui da sei mesi); per + passato prossimo; fa; da quanto tempo...?

chapters.a_plot: Ben writes his first Italian CV for a marketing job in Milan, then wonders if he wants it. He has worked at the bar for two months.
chapters.b_plot: Roberto has been president of the committee for twelve years. Marina asks him when he'll stop.
chapters.runner: Ornella: 'Abito in questa strada da cinquantadue anni.'

grammar.name: Verbs + a / di + infinitive
grammar.scope: cominciare a, continuare a, imparare a, aiutare a; finire di, decidere di, cercare di, provare a, smettere di, ricordarsi di

chapters.a_plot: The committee forces Ben and Roberto to co-organise the Festa dei Tigli. Rival plans, a stolen sound system, and then, somehow, the best festa in years.
chapters.b_plot: Emma and Tommaso try to spend the evening together without their fathers noticing.
chapters.arc: Tentpole: the Festa dei Tigli, while the lindens bloom. Ben–Roberto: a first grudging respect.

title.en: In Italy, That's How It's Done

grammar.name: Impersonal si
grammar.scope: si + third-person singular verb for general statements (si mangia, non si fa); si + plural noun agreement as a preview

chapters.a_plot: Ben writes a list of 'Italian rules' for his cookbook: no cappuccino after 11, no pineapple on pizza, no leaving the table. Franco corrects every one, and adds ten more.
chapters.b_plot: Samira and Lucia plan the baby shower (not an Italian tradition). What is done and not done in two cultures.
chapters.runner: Leo breaks every rule on the list in one day.

grammar.name: Indefinite adjectives and pronouns
grammar.scope: qualcuno, qualcosa, ognuno, ogni, tutto/tutti, alcuni, qualche + singular, nessuno, altro, molti/pochi

chapters.a_plot: Summer plans: everyone wants something different. Chiara wants the mountains, Ben the beach, Emma to stay home (with Tommaso), and Leo to go everywhere.
chapters.b_plot: The builders have gone on holiday. All of them. For all of August.
chapters.runner: Qualcuno has eaten all the gelato. Everyone suspects someone.

grammar.name: Necessity: bisogna, avere bisogno di, è necessario
grammar.scope: bisogna + infinitive; avere bisogno di + noun/infinitive; è necessario/importante + infinitive; mi fa male / mi fanno male

chapters.a_plot: Ben gets a terrible sunburn at the pool and has to go to the pharmacy, where Nadia is working. He tries to describe his symptoms; the whole queue helps.
chapters.b_plot: Nadia's check-up. Matteo comes with 30 questions written down, and the doctor needs only five minutes.

grammar.name: Ordinal numbers, years, centuries
grammar.scope: primo–decimo and -esimo; saying years (nel 1975); decades; il Novecento; floors (al secondo piano)

chapters.theme: History, the past of the house and street
chapters.a_plot: The last day of the works: inside the old kitchen wall the builders find a tin box with letters and photos from 1975. Whose are they?
chapters.b_plot: Ornella recognises the handwriting: the house used to belong to a family she knew. She tells Ben and Leo the street's history, from the first houses in 1962.
chapters.arc: Planted: the tin box connects to Anna and Franco's youth (it pays off in S3).

grammar.name: Review: passato prossimo and pronouns
grammar.scope: Consolidation of passato prossimo (avere/essere, irregulars, reflexives) with direct/indirect pronouns, ci and ne; telling the story of a season

chapters.a_plot: The house is finally finished. The first dinner in the new kitchen: everyone tells the story of the renovation, each version different.
chapters.b_plot: Late that night, Emma and Tommaso share their first kiss by the hedge, and Roberto sees it from his window.
chapters.arc: SEASON FINALE: home completed; Emma and Tommaso are out in the open (to Roberto, at least).
